This looks like February 2016. The unemployment rate is 4.9%, the fed funds rate is about 0.37%, and the 10-year yield is 1.76%. Credit spreads are wide, with Baa minus 10-year at 3.56, and the dollar is strong. Industrial production is slightly negative year on year, and gold rose 11.4% in the month, which fits February 2016. Equities were down over 3 months, with the S&P 500 up 2.4% over the month. Headline CPI of 1.34% also fits.

The one check against this is the S&P's 1-month return. February 2016 was roughly flat at -0.1%, while March 2016 was +6.8%. A +2.4% figure doesn't match either, so the snapshot may be a different month.

January 2016 was -5%, and the 3-month return of -7% fits February better. The 10-year yield was 1.74% at end-February and 1.78% at end-March. Gold rose 10% in February 2016 and fell in March, so February is the better match. Fed funds was 0.37% in February, and the unemployment rate was 4.9% in February.

I'll go with February 2016. The equity 1-month discrepancy is small enough that the data may use a slightly different series.
